title: Bridge chemistry — annotated impressions and probe list
body:
Context:
Quick, informal post-loop sketch capturing both subjective "chemistry" signals and concrete technical probes to use for follow-ups. Interview was for Senior Runtime Engineer (inbound from loop on 2026-02-19). This doc is intentionally terse — store as a personal synthesis to drive a focused follow-up ask and a short calibration with hiring panel.

One-line takeaway:
Candidate lands strongly on systems intuition and debug chops; weaker on distributed serving design tradeoffs and operational guardrails we expect for the role. Has growth potential but needs clear mentoring and a phased scope.

Raw impressions (verbatim-style, quick bullets):
- Calm thinker, pauses to build model before answering; uses examples rather than abstract platitudes.
- Excellent at single-node perf tuning: memory layout, kernel selection tradeoffs, profiling methodology (nvprof/trace ideas), and quantization pitfalls.
- When asked about cross-machine KV cache coherence and multi-tenant routing, answers skewed to theoretical rather than operational — fewer concrete fallback policies or failure-mode playbooks.
- Good code hygiene examples (tests, CI hooks, small diff examples). Demo'd a compact script to reproduce a nondeterministic memory leak — strong debugging pattern.
- Communication: concise to engineers, less practiced at explaining tradeoffs to product/pm-level audiences.
- Cultural fit: curious and humble; asked many clarifying questions (good sign).

Strengths (short):
- Profiling-first mindset; pragmatic microbench approach.
- Strong C++/CUDA instincts and a few shipping stories of latency wins.
- Observable-first instincts (logs, metrics, tracing).

Risks / gaps (short):
- Distributed runtime patterns (multi-host leasing, kv sharding, rebalancing) had conceptual answers but lacked concrete runbooks and SLO-first design examples.
- Limited experience owning 24x7 production SLAs or leading cross-team incident responses as primary pager.
- Prefers focused problem scope; may need coaching to broaden to platform-level tradeoffs (billing, multi-tenant fairness, rollout policies).

Suggested targeted probes for follow-up (use in a short synchronous session or take-home):
1) Give a scenario: replica imbalance in a dedicated pool causes tail latency spikes during periodic checkpointing. Ask candidate to write a runbook-style sequence: detection signal, automated mitigation steps, and postmortem actions. Score on concreteness and orchestration integration.
2) Provide a tiny pseudo-architecture: 3-region routing, two model variants (fast/cheap vs accurate/expensive), and burst traffic. Ask for concrete routing policy precedence and graceful fallback pseudocode. Look for cost-awareness and safety nets.
3) Present a nondeterministic memory growth reproduction snippet and ask them to outline a minimal automated test that would have caught the regression earlier (what to assert, CI hooks, perf baseline).
4) Ask for a stakeholder-communication blurb: explain a proposed change to quantization that could reduce cost by 30% but increase hallucination risk by small margin — how to frame to product + legal + CS.

Calibration rubric (quick numeric, for internal use):
- System design (distributed runtime): 3/5
- Perf/debugging: 5/5
- Operational ownership (SRE/executes on-call): 3/5
- Communication across teams (eng + product): 3/5
- Culture / learning curve: 4/5

Suggested hire plan and role entry path (if we advance):
- Consider hire at Senior (IC4) with intentional 6-month onboarding that pairs candidate with an SRE mentor and a platform architect.
- First 90 days: ship two measurable outcomes — (a) implement a detection+auto-mitigation for a tail-latency pattern in a staging pool, and (b) add a gating CI test for a class of memory regressions.
- Compensation band: align to Senior IC level; recommend hiring manager confirm match against internal comp spreadsheet JIRA-HIRE-1291.

Follow-up asks for candidate (if progressing to take-home or second loop):
- Short take-home: implement a small repro and a CI test for the memory leak scenario (timebox 4 hours, provide skeleton repo).
- Or, a 45-min focused loop with SRE lead and platform architect to evaluate design + ops language.

Calibration notes to share with panel (two sentences):
Candidate is high-signal for execution and low-level optimizer work; needs explicit operational ramp to be autonomous across our Dedicated and Private deployment guarantees. Recommend second touch focused on ops/runbook tradeoffs rather than another pure code screen.

Open questions / unresolved signals I want to clarify with the candidate or ref checks:
- Have they owned an on-call rotation where they were the person expected to write the postmortem and lead remediation?
- Depth of experience with multi-tenant fairness mechanisms (quotas, backpressure at router layer).
- Examples of influencing product/pm decisions when a perf vs quality tradeoff was present.

Quick action items (my notes):
- If panel leans yes: schedule 45m ops-focused loop with @Jonah and @Priya (suggest dates: 2026-02-25 or 2026-02-26).
- Draft a 4-hour take-home skeleton repo and checklist (I can prepare; reuse memory-leak skeleton from internal infra repo).
- Add a line in the candidate record highlighting "needs ops ramp" so IC hiring partner includes mentoring plan.

Mental model / note-to-self about calibration bias:
I value perf/debug chops highly because they map to immediate wins on runtime costs; adjust panel language to explicitly call this out so we don't undervalue ops gaps or over-index on kernel-fu alone.

End of note.
